Object Shallow Merge Behavior

Object Shallow Merge is a Merge behavior that combines object-based FeatureCell state values using a single-level merge strategy during the Merge stage.

This behavior treats objects as immutable values. When both the current state and the incoming value are plain objects, the incoming object is spread over the existing state, producing a new object where only the first-level properties are merged.

Nested objects are not merged recursively. If a nested property exists in the incoming value, it fully replaces the corresponding property in the current state. Non-object values, arrays, and null values bypass merging and are forwarded directly.

Object Shallow Merge runs within the core Merge stage and produces the merged candidate state passed to downstream pipeline stages. It does not mutate existing state, does not emit snapshots directly, and does not influence pipeline control flow beyond producing the merged value.

Note

The Merge stage is entered exclusively through explicit state-update APIs. Pipeline executions that invoke merge semantics are initiated via the mergeState method, which supply the incoming value and optional merge configuration used by the active Merge behavior.

Diagrams
Configuration

Object shallow merge behavior is configured as part of the Merge stage and defines how object-based FeatureCell state values are combined with incoming resolved values using single-level, structural merge semantics.

Exactly one merge behavior is active for a FeatureCell at any time. When withObjectShallowMergeBehavior is provided, it replaces the default merge strategy and becomes the active merge behavior for that FeatureCell.

Merge behaviors may be influenced by the clearUndefined configuration flag. When clearUndefined is enabled, an incoming undefined value is treated as an intentional clear request and results in the FeatureCell state being cleared. When disabled, incoming undefined values preserve the existing state and produce no merge output.

The clearUndefined option is supplied at the time a merge-style update is initiated and is evaluated by the active merge behavior during the Merge stage. It does not affect resolution, operators, or downstream pipeline stages.

Object shallow merge combines only the first level of plain-object properties. Nested objects are not merged recursively and are replaced in their entirety when present in the incoming value. Non-object values, arrays, and null values bypass merging and are forwarded directly.

Evaluation Outcomes

The Object Shallow Merge behavior evaluates the current committed FeatureCell state and the incoming resolved value to produce a single merged result during the Merge stage.

When both the current state and incoming value are plain objects, Object Shallow Merge performs a single-level merge. Properties from the incoming object overwrite properties on the existing state at the top level only. Nested objects are not merged recursively and are replaced in their entirety when present.

Non-object values—including primitives, arrays, and null—bypass merging and replace the existing state directly. Existing state is never mutated.

When the incoming value is undefined, merge behavior is controlled by the clearUndefined configuration option. This determines whether the existing state is preserved or intentionally cleared.

Example 1: Shallow Object Merge
Inputs Merged Result
current: { user: { id: 1, name: "Jane" }, active: true }

next: { user: { name: "Jane Doe" } }

 { user: { name: "Jane Doe" }, active: true } — nested object is replaced, not merged
Example 2: Non-Object Incoming Value
Inputs Merged Result
current: { count: 5 }

next: 9

 9 — incoming value replaces the existing state
Example 3: Null Incoming Value
Inputs Merged Result
current: { enabled: true }

next: null

 null — null replaces the existing state directly
Example 4: Undefined Incoming Value (Preserve)
Inputs Merged Result
current: { enabled: true }

next: undefined

clearUndefined: false

 { enabled: true } — existing state is preserved
Example 5: Undefined Incoming Value (Clear)
Inputs Merged Result
current: { enabled: true }

next: undefined

clearUndefined: true

 undefined — state is intentionally cleared
Examples

Example 1: Use the withObjectShallowMergeBehavior in a FeatureCell

This example demonstrates a FeatureCell configured with the withObjectShallowMergeBehavior. Incoming values provided via mergeState are merged at the top level only. When a property exists in both the current state and the incoming value, the incoming property replaces the existing one entirely.

Shallow merge does not recursively combine nested objects. If a nested object is provided in the incoming value, it replaces the corresponding nested object on the existing state rather than merging its fields.

Note

When a custom merge behavior is supplied, it replaces the default withArrayMergeBehavior for that FeatureCell. Exactly one merge behavior is active at any time. 

{{`// app.config.ts

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService
      {
        key: 'employee-profile',
        initialState: {
          user: {
            id: 1,
            name: 'Jane',
            preferences: {
              theme: 'light'
            }
          },
          active: true
        }
      },
      [
        // Explicitly attach the Object Shallow Merge behavior
        withObjectShallowMergeBehavior
      ]
    )
  ]
};

// bank-employee.service.ts

import { Injectable } from '@angular/core';
import { FeatureCell, injectVault } from '@sdux-vault/angular';
import { EmployeeProfile } from './employee-profile.shape';

@FeatureCell<EmployeeProfile>('employee-profile')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  readonly vault = injectVault<EmployeeProfile>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault.initialize();
  }

  updateEmployee(): void {
    this.vault.mergeState({
      value: {
        user: {
          name: 'Jane Doe'
        }
      }
    });
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<EmployeeProfile>(
  {
    key: 'employee-profile',
    initialState: {
      user: {
        id: 1,
        name: 'Jane',
        preferences: {
          theme: 'light'
        }
      },
      active: true
    },
  },
  [
    // Explicitly attach the Object Shallow Merge behavior
    withObjectShallowMergeBehavior
  ]
);

// Initialize the FeatureCell
employeeCell.initialize();

// Shallow-merge a top-level update
employeeCell.mergeState({
  value: {
    user: {
      name: 'Jane Doe'
    }
  }
});`}}
